name: Wang Zhaochun
current_role: Co-founder, legal representative and co-controlling shareholder of Zhuhai Bojay Electronics (Bojay, SZSE: 002975); chairman per 2025-26 filings/press
profile: Wang Zhaochun (b. 1972) co-founded Zhuhai Bojay Electronics, a maker of automated test and assembly equipment for electronics (Apple-chain supplier), listed in Shenzhen in 2020. He is one of three controlling shareholders acting in concert with Fu Lin and Cheng Jun.
interesting_fact: Bojay's three founders (Wang Zhaochun, Fu Lin, Cheng Jun) jointly control the company as concert parties, holding stakes partly via the Bohang, Bowang and Bozhan investment partnerships that Wang manages.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bojay, Wang worked in a knitting factory and a machinery factory in Zhuhai from 1989 to 1997, then ran his own small machinery-and-mould workshop.
notes: Sources disagree on whether he is still chairman (one profile says chair term ended June 2024; 2025 report lists him as legal representative, 2026 press calls him chairman). Board secretary Huang Can handles investor contact. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Pan Yejiang
profile: Pan Yejiang (b. 1977, master's degree) is the actual controller of VATTI, the Zhongshan, Guangdong kitchen-appliance maker (range hoods, gas hobs, water heaters). Formerly chairman/GM of Guangdong Baide Group, he has chaired VATTI since 2015 and runs it as chairman and president, holding ~87m shares directly.
interesting_fact: As official sponsor of France's team, VATTI promised full refunds on 'champion' packages bought June 1-July 3, 2018 if France won the World Cup; France did, costing an estimated RMB 79m (~$12m), which the company said was within its marketing budget.
deep_cut_fact: Before taking VATTI's chair he ran Guangdong Baide Group as chairman and general manager; he also chairs the investment firm Guangdong Deqian Investment Management.
notes: IR emails are the board secretary and securities representative contacts listed in VATTI's 2025 annual report summary. Wealth shared with Pan Quanzhi (relative). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Gao Xueming
current_role: Founder, Chairman and legal representative, Luoyang Northglass Technology Co. (SZSE: 002613)
profile: Gao Xueming (b. 1958), a senior engineer, founded Luoyang Northglass Technology in 1995. The company makes glass deep-processing equipment, notably tempering furnaces, and processed glass, and listed in Shenzhen in 2011. He remains chairman and controlling shareholder, acting in concert with Feng Jinjun and Gao Xuelin.
interesting_fact: Gao is an engineer-founder: he spent 12 years at state-owned Luoyang Glass, rising from technician to engineer, senior engineer and branch-factory head, before starting Northglass in 1995.
deep_cut_fact: Northglass began in 1995 as Luoyang Northglass Technology Co., Ltd., founded by Gao after his 1982-1994 stint at Luoyang Glass Factory, where he ended as a branch-factory director.
notes: Hurun listing (2015-17) is older. Still chairman per the 2025 annual report (April 2026). The IR mailbox is a 126.com address, as published by the company. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Talal Jassim Al-Bahar
current_role: Vice Chairman & CEO, Kuwait Real Estate Co. (AQARAT); Chairman & Group CEO, IFA Hotels & Resorts; Chairman, Arzan Financial Group; Independent Director, Miami International Holdings (MIAX)
profile: Kuwaiti investor and real-estate/hospitality executive with a Loyola Marymount business degree. He led International Financial Advisors and Kuwait Invest Holding, now runs AQARAT and IFA Hotels & Resorts, chairs Arzan Financial Group, and has long sat on the board of US options-exchange operator MIAX, where his stake is worth ~$300m.
interesting_fact: In January 2025 AQARAT and IFA Hotels & Resorts launched the $953m Al Tay Hills residential project in Sharjah, which reportedly sold about $572m in its first week; Forbes Middle East ranked him No. 42 among the region's most impactful real-estate leaders of 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He is credited as the driving force behind IFA Hotels & Resorts' global expansion, which tripled in size under him, and he is a certified Six Sigma Development Champion.
notes: The MIAX IR contact goes to a company where he is only a director. A more direct route is likely via AQARAT, Arzan or IFA Hotels & Resorts corporate offices in Kuwait. He also sits on the Boursa Kuwait board.

name: Shao Yutian
current_role: Founder of Zhejiang Nanyang Technology (now CASC Rainbow, 002389); private investor whose family backs capacitor-film maker Xingyang Technology and other firms
profile: Shao Yutian founded Zhejiang Nanyang Electronic Film Co. in Taizhou in 2001. It became Nanyang Technology, a maker of capacitor and optical films, and listed in Shenzhen in 2010. A 2016-17 restructuring merged in CASC's drone assets (now CASC Rainbow) and cut his stake to ~3%. His family has since backed Xingyang Technology's Beijing Stock Exchange IPO filing and invested across the solar supply chain.
interesting_fact: The capacitor-film company he started in 2001 became, via a 2016-17 asset restructuring, CASC Rainbow (Aerospace CH UAV), China's listed maker of Rainbow military drones.
notes: No published personal or office contact found. He no longer controls a listed company. Recent coverage (2024-25) concerns family investments in Xingyang Tech and Taifu Pump's 2025 related-party acquisition of Nanyang Huacheng. Hurun listing is old (2010-18). Activity was reported in 2024-25, but there is no explicit confirmation he is alive. Wealth is shared with son Shao Yixing.

name: Lord Alli (Waheed Alli)
current_role: Labour life peer (Baron Alli of Norbury), House of Lords; media entrepreneur and investor
profile: Waheed Alli (b. 1964, Croydon) left school at 16 and co-founded TV producer Planet 24 (The Big Breakfast, The Word, Survivor format) with Charlie Parsons. He later chaired Chorion (Agatha Christie, Enid Blyton rights) and ASOS, and ran Silvergate Media (Octonauts, Peter Rabbit) until 2022. A Labour peer since 1998, he remains active in the Lords.
interesting_fact: Made a life peer in 1998 at 33, he was one of the youngest members of the Lords and one of the few openly gay Muslim politicians in the world. He campaigned to repeal Section 28 and to equalise the age of consent.
deep_cut_fact: His first job after leaving school at 16 with nine O-levels was junior researcher at a finance magazine. He went on to serve as Chancellor of De Montfort University (2006-2015).
notes: The email is the House of Lords' generic member-contact address listed on his parliamentary profile (House of Lords, London SW1A 0PW). He is politically sensitive: he was at the centre of the 2024 Labour donations/gifts row and a Lords standards inquiry found a registration breach, so outreach should be framed carefully.

name: Catherine Zeta-Jones
current_role: Actor and producer (e.g. Wednesday S2 on Netflix, Kill Jackie on Prime Video as star/executive producer, The Gallerist); founder of Casa Zeta-Jones lifestyle brand
profile: Swansea-born actor (b. 1969) who rose from West End musicals to Hollywood stardom (The Mask of Zorro, Traffic, Chicago). She won the Oscar, BAFTA and SAG for Chicago and a Tony for A Little Night Music. Her wealth is shared with husband Michael Douglas. She launched the Casa Zeta-Jones home brand in 2017 and still acts and produces.
interesting_fact: She is one of the few performers to have won both an Academy Award (Chicago, 2003) and a Tony Award (A Little Night Music, 2010), and was made a CBE in 2010 for film and charity work.
deep_cut_fact: Her break came in 1987 as the second understudy in 42nd Street in the West End. When the star and first understudy were both unavailable she went on as Peggy Sawyer, and the producer kept her in the role for two years. She was made a Freeman of Swansea in 2019.
notes: A Hollywood celebrity, not an entrepreneur in energy/data centres. The realistic route is her talent agency or publicist (not verified here) or Casa Zeta-Jones. Rich-list wealth is joint with Michael Douglas.

name: Dame Janet de Botton
current_role: Chairman of the Board, The Wolfson Foundation
profile: Janet Wolfson de Botton, eldest daughter of Lord (Leonard) Wolfson and granddaughter of GUS founder Sir Isaac Wolfson, is a London art collector and philanthropist. She was a Tate trustee and chair of the Tate Modern council, and has chaired the Wolfson Foundation since 2010. Her wealth is inherited plus that of her late husband, financier Gilbert de Botton (Global Asset Management).
interesting_fact: In 1996 she gave Tate 60 contemporary works, including Warhol, Cindy Sherman and Richard Long, and in 2010 she donated a Cy Twombly ceiling painting to the Louvre's Salle des Bronzes. She was made a Dame (DBE) in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: She is a serious competitive bridge player whose record appears in World Bridge Federation and European Bridge League results.
notes: Very private philanthropist. Best route is the Wolfson Foundation communications team. Contacts belong to the foundation, not her personally. The web-search budget ran out here, so the bridge detail is general rather than a specific title.

name: Michael Kirban
current_role: Co-Founder and Executive Chairman, The Vita Coco Company (Nasdaq: COCO)
profile: Michael Kirban co-founded Vita Coco with Ira Liran in 2004 and built it into the leading US coconut-water brand. Vita Coco also sells Copra, private-label coconut water and other drinks, IPO'd on Nasdaq in 2021, and is a public benefit corporation and Certified B Corp. As executive chairman he continues to steer the company, whose sales and EBITDA grew strongly in 2026.
interesting_fact: The company began after a 2003 conversation in a New York bar with two Brazilian women who said coconut water was what they missed most from home. Liran later married one of them and moved to Brazil, and Kirban's visit there sparked the business.
deep_cut_fact: In the early days Kirban roller-skated through New York neighbourhoods selling Vita Coco and handing out samples himself.
notes: IR is handled by ICR, Inc. He is a relatively media-friendly founder who often speaks at consumer/entrepreneurship events. The web-search budget ran out, so personal social accounts were not verified.

name: Iain Anderson
current_role: Chairman, GAP Group / GAP Hire Solutions (Glasgow)
profile: Iain Anderson is the son of Gordon Anderson, who founded Gordon Anderson Plant in Glasgow in 1969. He joined the family business in 1984 and, with brother Douglas, built it into GAP Hire Solutions, which calls itself the UK's largest independent family-owned hire company (~200 locations, ~£200m revenue by 2019). He is chairman, and the third generation (his son James, daughter Nicola, nephew Mark) now holds senior roles.
interesting_fact: GAP grew from a single plant-hire firm (Gordon Anderson Plant, 1969) into a national hire group with almost 200 depots, including Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man. It was renamed GAP Group in 1999.
deep_cut_fact: Iain joined his father's plant-hire firm in 1984. In 2019, the year that would have been founder Gordon Anderson's 100th birthday, GAP opened its largest-ever depot at Tilbury. The company also runs a charity programme, GAP Giving.
notes: Private family company with a low media profile. Its pump/power division (generators) may be relevant to the energy angle. Identity is inferred from rich-list 'plant hire' shared with Douglas Anderson plus GAP's published history. The web-search budget ran out, so no independent press check was done.

name: John C. Hadjipateras
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Dorian LPG Ltd. (NYSE: LPG)
profile: A Greek shipping veteran (age 76), Hadjipateras has managed shipping companies since 1972. He ran Peninsular Maritime in London (1972-92), then led Eagle Ocean, and in 2013 founded Dorian LPG, an owner of very large gas carriers (VLGCs) moving LPG worldwide. He remains chairman and CEO and recently reported record earnings on strong freight markets.
interesting_fact: He has been a member of the Baltic Exchange since 1972 and has served on the Greek Shipping Co-operation Committee and the INTERTANKO Council. He was also a director of SEACOR Holdings.
deep_cut_fact: He was a trustee of the UK children's charity Kidscape for forty years and sat on the Board of Advisors of Georgetown University's Faculty of Languages and Linguistics. He is now a trustee of the Hellenic American Cultural Foundation.
notes: IR contact is CFO Ted Young (Stamford, CT office). Strong energy-shipping angle (LPG/ammonia-capable carriers) for an energy podcast.

name: Sanjay Govil
current_role: Founder and CEO, Zyter (AI workflow platform); founder/chairman, Infinite Computer Solutions; owner, Washington Freedom (Major League Cricket)
profile: An Indian-American tech entrepreneur, Govil studied electrical engineering at Auburn, did graduate study at Syracuse and Wharton, and started at IBM. He founded IT-services firm Infinite Computer Solutions in 1999 (taken private in 2018). He now runs Zyter, an agentic-AI platform for healthcare and utilities, and is a major cricket investor.
interesting_fact: He is a founding investor in Major League Cricket and owns the Washington Freedom. In 2025 he bought a 50% stake in The Hundred's Welsh Fire for about $50m.
deep_cut_fact: Long before cricket, he owned the Delhi Acers franchise in India's Premier Badminton League, before selling it to the Dalmia Group ahead of the 2017-18 season.
notes: Zyter lists utilities as a target industry, which fits the energy/AI angle. The X account belongs to his cricket team, not to him personally. Based in the Washington DC area. The web-search budget ran out, so personal LinkedIn/X were not verified.
